Everyone can easily understand how great the hardship of the subjects must have been in amassing so

o: ammassare una sì grande quantità di frumentone, e di Caccao; massimamente dovendo procacciarsi il caccao pel commercio co' paesi caldi, non essendovi in tutto il regno d' Acolhuacan terreno proprio per la cultura di questa pianta. Mezzo l' anno, ovvero per nove mesi Messicani fornivano tal provvisione quattordici Città, ed altre quindici la provvisione dell' altro mezzo anno. s1 Ai giovani era addossata la provvision delle legna, che si consumavano nel Real Palagio in quantità sorprendente. I progressi fatti da questo celebre Re nelle arti, e nelle scienze furono tanti, quanti far si possono da un grand' ingegno, che non ha nè libri, in cui studiare, nè Maestri, da cui imparare. Er' abile nella Poesìa di quelle Nazioni, e fece varie composizioni, che furono universalmente applaudite. Nel secolo XVI. erano celebri, anche fra gli Spagnuoli, i sessanta Inni da lui composti in lode del Creator del Cielo. Due delle sue ode o canzoni, volgarizzate in verso spagnuolo dal suo discendente Don Ferdinando d' Alba Ixtlilxochitl, si son conservate insin' a' nostri tempi. s2 Una d' esse composta fu da lui qualche tempo dopo la rovina d' Azcapozalco. Il suo argomento non dissimile da quell' altro, di cui abbiam fatto già menzione, è quello di piangere l' instabilità della grandezza umana sulla persona del Tiranno Tezozomoc, il quale a guisa d' un albero grande, e folto avea distese per tanti paesi le sue radici, ed ampliati i suoi verdi rami sin' ad ombrare tutte le terre dell' Imperio; ma al fine intarlato e guasto cadde in terra senza veruna speranza di riprender la sua pristina verdura.
e: so great a quantity of maize and cacao; especially since the cacao had Bk. IV. to be procured through commerce with the hot countries, there being in the whole kingdom of Acolhuacan no land suited to the cultivation of this plant. For half the year, that is, for nine Mexican months, fourteen cities supplied this provision, and another fifteen the provision of the other half of the year. (g) To the young men was assigned the provision of the firewood, which was consumed in the royal palace in surprising quantity. The progress made by this celebrated king in the arts and in the sciences was as great as can be made by a great mind that has neither books in which to study nor masters from whom to learn. He was skilled in the poetry of those nations, and made various compositions that were universally applauded. In the sixteenth century the sixty hymns composed by him in praise of the Creator of Heaven were famous even among the Spaniards. Two of his odes or songs, rendered into Spanish verse by his descendant Don Fernando de Alva Ixtlilxochitl, have been preserved down to our own times. (h) One of them was composed by him some time after the ruin of Azcapotzalco. Its subject, not unlike that of the other of which we have already made mention, is to lament the instability of human greatness in the person of the Tyrant Tezozomoc, who, like a great and thick tree, had spread his roots through so many countries and extended his green branches so far as to shade all the lands of the empire; but at last, worm-eaten and spoiled, fell to the ground without any hope of recovering his former greenness.

o: Ma in nulla dilettavasi tanto Nezahualcojotl, quanto nello studio della natura. Acquistò pure parecchie cognizioni astronomiche colla frequente osservazione, che faceva del corso degli astri. S' applicò altresì a conoscere le piante, e gli animali, e perchè non poteva tener nella sua Corte quelli, ch' erano proprj di diverso clima, fece dipingere al vivo ne' suoi palagj tutti i vegetabili ed animali della terra d' Anahuac: delle quali dipinture ne fa testimonianza il celebre Dottor Hernandez, che le vide, ed in parte se ne servì. Dipinture in vero assai più utili, e più degne d' un Real palagio, di quelle che rappresentano la scellerata mitologìa de' Greci. Investigava curiosamente le cagioni degli effetti, che ammirava nella natura, e questa continua osservazione gli fece conoscere la sciocchezza della idolatrìa. A' suoi figliuoli diceva privatamente, che nell' adorar esteriormente gl' idoli per conformarsi col Popolo, detestassero coll' animo quel culto degno di scherno, perchè diretto a creature insensate: ch' egli altro Dio non riconosceva, se non il Creator del Cielo, e che non vietava nel suo regno, come vorrebbe, l' Idolatrìa, per non esser biasimato di voler contraddire alla dottrina de' suoi maggiori. Proibì i sacrifizj d' umane vittime; ma accorgendosi poi, quanto sia malagevole il distornar una Nazione dalle idee antiche in materia di religione, tornò a permetterli, ma comandando sotto gravi pene, che non fossero mai sacrificati altri, che i prigionieri di guerra. Fabbricò ad onor del Creator del Cielo un' alta torre di nove piani, L' ultimo piano era oscuro con una piccola volta dipinta al di dentro di turchino, ed ornata di cornici d' oro. Risiedevano sempre in questa torre degli uomini incaricati di sonare in certe ore del giorno delle lame di finissimo metallo, al suono delle quali s' inginocchiava il Re per far la sua preghiera al Creator del Cielo, e ad onor di tal Dio faceva in certo tempo dell' anno un digiuno. s1
e: But in nothing did Nezahualcoyotl delight so much as in the study of Bk. IV. nature. He also acquired several astronomical notions by the frequent observation that he made of the course of the stars. He applied himself likewise to knowing the plants and the animals, and because he could not keep in his court those that were proper to a different clime, he had all the vegetables and animals of the land of Anahuac painted from life in his palaces; of which paintings the celebrated Dr. Hernández bears witness, who saw them and made use of them in part. Paintings truly far more useful and more worthy of a royal palace than those that represent the wicked mythology of the Greeks. He curiously investigated the causes of the effects that he admired in nature, and this continual observation made him recognize the folly of idolatry. To his sons he said privately that, in outwardly adoring the idols to conform with the people, they should detest in their minds that worship, worthy of scorn, because it was directed to insensible creatures; that he acknowledged no other God than the Creator of Heaven, and that he did not forbid idolatry in his kingdom, as he would wish, so as not to be blamed for wanting to contradict the doctrine of his ancestors. He prohibited sacrifices of human victims; but, perceiving afterward how difficult it is to turn a nation away from its ancient ideas in matters of religion, he returned to permitting them, but commanding under heavy penalties that no others should ever be sacrificed than prisoners of war. He built in honor of the Creator of Heaven a lofty tower of nine stories. The last story was dark, with a small vault painted on the inside with blue and adorned with gold moldings. There always resided in this tower men charged with sounding, at certain hours of the day, plates of very fine metal, at the sound of which the king knelt to make his prayer to the Creator of Heaven, and in honor of that God he made at a certain time of the year a fast. (i)

o: L' alto ingegno di questo Re spinto dal grande amore, che portava al suo Popolo, illustrò in cotal maniera la sua Corte, che nell' avvenire fu considerata, come la patria delle arti, ed il centro della cultura. Tezcuco era la Città, dove si parlava con maggior pulitezza, e perfezione la lingua Messicana, dove si trovavano i migliori Artefici, e dove più abbondavano i Poeti, gli Oratori, e gli Storici. s1 Quindi presero molte leggi i Messicani, ed altri Popoli: onde potrebbe dirsi Tezcuco essere stata l' Atene, e Nezahualcojotl il Solone d' Anahuac. Nella ultima sua malattia, avendo fatto venir alla sua presenza tutti i suoi figlj, dichiarò suo erede e successore nel regno d' Acolhuacan Nezahualpilli, il quale contuttochè fosse il più giovane di tutti, fu pure agli altri preposto così per essere nato dalla Regina Matlalcihuatzin, come per la sua notoria dirittura, e pel suo singolar talento. Incaricò il suo primogenito Acapipioltzin d' ajutar col suo consiglio il nuovo Re, finattantochè imparasse l' arte difficile di governare. A Nezahualpilli raccomandò caldamente l' amor dei suoi fratelli, la cura de' suoi sudditi, ed il zelo per la giustizia. Finalmente per impedir qualunque scompiglio, che dalla nuova della sua morte potesse cagionarsi, comandò, che si celasse, quanto possibil fosse, al Popolo, finchè Nezahualpilli assicurato fosse nel pacifico possesso della corona. I Principi accolsero con lagrime gli ultimi avvisi di loro Padre, e venendo fuori nella sala d' udienza, dove gli aspettava la Nobiltà, fu Nezahualpilli acclamato Re di Acolhuacan, dichiarando Acapipioltzin, esser questa la volontà di loro Padre, il quale avendo a fare un lungo viaggio, volle prima nominar ll suo successore. Diedero tutti l' ubbidienza al nuovo Re, e la mattina seguente morì Nezahualcojotl nel quarantesimo quarto anno del suo regno, e nell' ottantesimo incirca della sua età. I suoi figlj celarono la sua morte, ed
e: The lofty genius of this king, impelled by the great love that he bore Bk. IV. his people, so illustrated his court that in the future it was considered the homeland of the arts and the center of civilization. Texcoco was the city where the Mexican language was spoken with the greatest polish and perfection, where the best artisans were found, and where poets, orators, and historians were most abundant. (k) Hence the Mexicans and other peoples took many laws: wherefore it might be said that Texcoco had been the Athens, and Nezahualcoyotl the Solon, of Anahuac. In his last illness, having had all his sons come into his presence, he declared as his heir and successor in the kingdom of Acolhuacan Nezahualpilli, who, although he was the youngest of all, was nevertheless preferred to the others, both for having been born of Queen Matlalcihuatzin and for his well-known rectitude and his singular talent. He charged his eldest son Acapipioltzin to aid the new king with his counsel until he should learn the difficult art of governing. To Nezahualpilli he warmly recommended love of his brothers, care of his subjects, and zeal for justice. Finally, to prevent any disorder that the news of his death might cause, he commanded that it be concealed from the people, as far as possible, until Nezahualpilli should be secure in the peaceful possession of the crown. The princes received with tears the last counsels of their father, and, coming out into the audience hall, where the nobility awaited them, Nezahualpilli was acclaimed king of Acolhuacan, Acapipioltzin declaring that this was the will of their father, who, having a long journey to make, wished first to name his successor. All gave obedience to the new king, and the next morning Nezahualcoyotl died, in the forty-fourth year of his reign and about the eightieth of his age. His sons kept his death secret, and hid

o: occultarono il suo cadavero, bruciandolo segretamente, com' è da credersi, ed in vece di fargli le esequie, celebrarono con feste ed allegrezze straordinarie l' incoronazione del nuovo Re. Ma a dispetto delle loro diligenze, si sparse subito la nuova della sua morte per tutta la terra, e molti Signori vennero alla Corte a condolersi co' Principi. Nondimeno il volgo restò persuaso, che fosse stato quel gran Re trasferito alla compagnia degli Dei in premio delle sue virtù. [margin: §. 26. Conquista di Tlatelolco, e morte del Re Moquihuix.] Poco tempo dopo l' esaltazione di Nezahualpilli accadde la memorabil guerra de' Messicani co' loro vicini e rivali i Tlatelolchi. Il Re di Tlatelolco Moquihuix, non potendo sopportare la gloria del Messicano, adoperava tutti i mezzi per oscurarla. Era egli ammogliato, come abbiam già detto, con una sorella del Re Axajacatl, datagli da Motezuma in premio della famosa vittoria ottenuta sopra i Cotastesi. In questa sfortunata Signora sfogava spesso la sua rabbia contro il Cognato, e non contento di ciò procurò nascostamente allearsi con alrri stati, che portavano mal volentieri il giogo de' Messicani. Questi furono quei di Chalco, di Xilotepec, di Toltitlan, di Tenajucan, di Mexicaltzinco, di Huitzilopochco, di Xochimilco, di Cuitlahuac, e di Mizquic, i quali s' accordarono d' attaccar alle spalle i Messicani, dapoichè avessero cominciata la battaglia i Tlatelolchi. I Quauhpanchesi poi, gli Huexotzinchi, ed i Matlatzinchi, l' ajuto de' quali avea anche implorato, doveano incorporar le lor truppe a quelle de' Tlatelolchi per la difesa della Città. Seppe la Regina queste negoziazioni, ed ora per l' odio, che portava al suo marito, ora per l' amore a suo fratello, ed alla sua patria, avvisò di tutto Axajacatl, acciocchè schivasse un sì fatto colpo, che avrebbe fatto crollar il suo trono. Moquihuix, assicurato dell' ajuto de' Confederati, convocò i Nobili della sua Corte per incoraggirgli all' impresa. Alzò la voce nell' assemblea un Sacerdote vecchio ed autorevole, appellato Pojahuitl, ed a nome di tutti s' esibì a combatter coraggiosamente contro i nemici della patria:
e: his body, burning it secretly, as is to be believed, and instead of hold‐ Bk. IV. ing funeral rites for him, celebrated with extraordinary festivities and rejoicings the coronation of the new king. But in spite of their efforts the news of his death spread at once through the whole land, and many lords came to the court to condole with the princes. Nevertheless the common people remained persuaded that that great king had been transported to the company of the gods as a reward for his virtues. § 16. Not long after the exaltation of Nezahualpilli there occurred the Conquest of Tlatelolco, and death memorable war of the Mexicans with their neighbors and rivals the of King Moquihuix. Tlatelolcas. The king of Tlatelolco, Moquihuix, unable to bear the glory of the Mexican, used every means to obscure it. He was married, as we have already said, to a sister of King Axayacatl, given to him by Moctezuma as a reward for the famous victory won over the people of Cotaxtla. On this unfortunate lady he often vented his rage against his brother-in-law, and, not content with this, he secretly sought to ally himself with other states that bore the yoke of the Mexicans unwillingly. These were the people of Chalco, of Xilotepec, of Toltitlan, of Tenayuca, of Mexicaltzinco, of Huitzilopochco, of Xochimilco, of Cuitlahuac, and of Mixquic, who agreed to attack the Mexicans in the rear after the Tlatelolcas had begun the battle. The people of Cuauhpanco, moreover, the Huexotzincas, and the Matlatzincas, whose help he had also implored, were to incorporate their troops with those of the Tlatelolcas for the defense of the city. The queen learned of these negotiations, and, now from the hatred that she bore her husband, now from love of her brother and her country, she warned Axayacatl of everything, that he might avoid so serious a blow, which would have made his throne totter. Moquihuix, assured of the help of the confederates, convoked the nobles of his court to encourage them to the undertaking. An old and authoritative priest, called Poyahuitl, raised his voice in the assembly, and in the name of all offered to fight courageously against the enemies of the country: then

o: indi per animargli davvantaggio, lavò l' altare de' sacrifizj, e diede a bere quell' acqua tinta di sangue umano al Re, ed a tutti i Capitani, colla quale sentirono, per quel che dissero, aumentarsi il loro coraggio, ed io non dubito, che si fosse aumentato per esercitar della crudeltà. Frattanto la Regina impaziente del maltrattamento, che soffriva, ed impaurita da' perigli della guerra, lasciò il marito, e portossi a Messico con quattro figliuoli, per mettersi sotto l' ombra del suo fratello. Ciò far potè facilmente per la somma vicinanza di quelle due Città, Una tal novità accrebbe in tal maniera lo scambievol disgusto de' Messicani e de' Tlatelolchi, che dovunque s' incontravano, s' ingiuriavano con parole, si battevano, e s' ammazzavano. Accostandosi ormai il tempo di far la guerra, fece Moquihuix insieme co' suoi Capitani, e con molti de' Confederati un solenne sacrifizio nel monte men discosto dalla Città per procacciarsi la protezione de' loro Dei; ed ivi si determinò il giorno, nel quale dovea dichiararsi la guerra ai Messicacani. Indi a pochi giorni avvisò i Confederati, acciocchè fossero ben disposti a soccorergli, tosto che cominciasse l' attacco. Xiloman, Signor di Colhuacan, voleva assalire prima i Messicani, e poi simulando fuga provocargli ad inseguirlo, acciocchè allora i Tlatelolchi gli attaccassero per le spalle. Il giorno seguente queste ambasciate fece Moquihuix la ceremonia d' armar le sue truppe, ed indi portossi al tempio di Huitzilopochtli per implorar l' ajuto di lui, dove tornarono a prender quella abominabile bevanda, che diede a loro Pojahuitl nel primo congresso, e tutti i Soldati passarono ad uno ad uno dinanzi all' Idolo, facendogli una profonda riverenza. Appena terminata questa ceremonia entrò nella piazza del Mercato una compagnìa d' arditi Messicani, uccidendo tutti quanti incontravano; ma sopravvenendo subito le truppe Tlatelolche, gli scacciarono, e fecero alcuni prigionieri, i quali furono senza indugio sacrificati in un tempio appellato Tlillan. Quello stesso giorno sul tramontar del Sole ebbero alcune donne Tlatelolche l' ardire d' innoltrarsi nelle strade di
e: to encourage them still further, he washed the altar of the sacrifices Bk. IV. and gave that water, tinged with human blood, to the king and to all the captains to drink; with it, they said, they felt their courage grow, and I do not doubt that it had grown the better to practice cruelty. Meanwhile the queen, impatient of the ill treatment she suffered and frightened by the perils of the war, left her husband and betook herself to Mexico with four children, to put herself under the shelter of her brother. This she could do easily because of the very short distance between the two cities. Such a novelty so increased the mutual ill feeling of the Mexicans and the Tlatelolcas that wherever they met they insulted one another with words, came to blows, and killed one another. As the time for making war was now drawing near, Moquihuix, together with his captains and many of the confederates, held a solemn sacrifice on the mountain least distant from the city, in order to obtain the protection of their gods; and there the day was fixed on which war was to be declared on the Mexicans. A few days later he gave notice to the confederates, so that they might be well prepared to come to his aid as soon as the attack began. Xiloman, lord of Colhuacan, wished first to assail the Mexicans and then, feigning flight, to provoke them to pursue him, so that the Tlatelolcas might attack them from behind. The day after these embassies Moquihuix performed the ceremony of arming his troops, and then betook himself to the temple of Huitzilopochtli to implore his help; there they returned to drink that abominable draught which Poyahuitl had given them at the first assembly, and all the soldiers passed one by one before the idol, making it a deep reverence. No sooner was this ceremony over than a company of bold Mexicans entered the market square, killing everyone they met; but the Tlatelolca troops, coming up at once, drove them out and took some prisoners, who were sacrificed without delay in a temple called Tlillan. That same day, at sunset, some Tlatelolca women had the boldness to advance into the streets of

o: Messico, e di bruciar delle scope nelle porte delle case, dicendo sfacciatamente degl' improperj a' Messicani, e minacciandogli della lor pronta ruina; ma i Messicani le trattarono col disprezzo, che meritavano. Quella stessa notte si misero in arme i Tlatelolchi, e la mattina cominciarono alla prima luce l' attacco di Messico. Erano nel maggior caldo della zuffa, quando arrivò Xiloman co' suoi Colhui; ma vedendo che il Re di Tlatelolco aveva cominciato a combattere senza aspettarlo, nè curarsi del consiglio di lui, si ritirò sdegnato, e volendo far qualche danno a' Messicani, fece chiuder alcuni canali per impedir ogni soccorso, che venir potesse a loro per acqua; ma furono tosto riaperti per ordine d' Axajacatl. Tutto quel dì si combattè con indicibile ardore e dall' una, e dall' altra parte, finchè la notte costrinse i Tlatelolchi a ritirarsi. I Messicani bruciarono le case della Città, che erano più vicine a Tlatelolco, perchè forse gl' impacciavano per i combattimenti; ma nell' appicciar il fuoco venti di loro furono fatti prigioni da' nemici, ed incontanente sacrificati. Axajacatl distribuì quella notte il suo esercito in tutte le strade, che conducevano a Tlatelolco, ed allo spuntar del dì cominciarono da ogni parte a marciare verso la piazza del mercato, che dovea esser il punto della loro riunione. I Tlatelolchi, vedendosi da ogni parte attaccati, si andavano ritirando verso quella gran piazza, per unir ivi tutte le loro forze, e poter vieppiù resistere; ma arrivati a quel luogo si trovarono più impacciati dalla stessa loro moltitudine. Non bastavano già le voci, colle quali il Re Moquihuix procurava dall' alto del gran tempio d' incoraggire i suoi. I Tlatelolchi erano feriti ed uccisi, e que' che cadevano, sfogavano la loro rabbia contro il Re con improperj: „ Scendete di costà, gli dicevano, e prendete, o Codardo, l' armi; poichè non è da uomini coraggiosi lo star guardando tranquillamente que' che combattono, e perdono la vita in difesa della patria. „ Ma questi lamenti cagionati dal dolor delle ferite, e dalle angoscie della morte, erano
e: Mexico and to burn brooms at the doors of the houses, shamelessly Bk. IV. hurling insults at the Mexicans and threatening them with their swift ruin; but the Mexicans treated them with the contempt they deserved. That same night the Tlatelolcas took up arms, and in the morning, at first light, they began the attack on Mexico. They were in the hottest of the fray when Xiloman arrived with his Colhuas; but seeing that the king of Tlatelolco had begun to fight without waiting for him, and without heeding his counsel, he withdrew in indignation, and, wishing to do the Mexicans some harm, had certain canals closed to prevent any relief that might reach them by water; but they were soon reopened by order of Axayacatl. All that day they fought with indescribable ardor on both sides, until night forced the Tlatelolcas to withdraw. The Mexicans burned the houses of the city that were nearest to Tlatelolco, perhaps because they hampered them in the fighting; but in setting the fire twenty of them were taken prisoner by the enemy and immediately sacrificed. Axayacatl that night distributed his army in all the streets that led to Tlatelolco, and at daybreak they began to march from every side toward the market square, which was to be the point of their union. The Tlatelolcas, seeing themselves attacked on every side, were falling back toward that great square, to unite all their forces there and be able to resist still better; but on arriving at that place they found themselves more hampered by their own multitude. The shouts with which King Moquihuix tried from the top of the great temple to encourage his men were of no avail. The Tlatelolcas were wounded and killed, and those who fell vented their rage against the king with insults: “Come down from there,” they said to him, “and take up arms, you coward; for it is not the part of brave men to stand calmly watching those who fight and lose their lives in defense of their homeland.” But these laments, caused by the pain of their wounds and the anguish of death, were

o: affatto ingiusti: poichè Moquihuix non mancava a' doveri di Generale, e di Re, non dovendo egli esporre tanto la sua, quanto i Soldati la loro vita, per poter esser ad essi più utile col consiglio, e colla voce. Frattanto i Messicani s' avanzarono fino alla scala del tempio, e salendo per essa, arrivarono all' atrio superiore, donde Moquihuix animava la sua gente, e si difendeva da disperato; ma un Capitano Messicano appellato Quetzalhua, con una spinta lo rovesciò giù per la scala, s1 ed alcuni Soldati togliendone sulle lor braccia il cadavero, lo presentarono ad Axajacatl, il quale apertogli il petto, gli strappò il cuore. Azione orribile, ma eseguita senza orrore, per esser troppo comune ne' loro sacrifizj. Così finì il prode Moquihuix, e con lui la piccola Monarchìa de' Tlatelolchi, governata da quattro Re nello spazio di cento diciotto anni incirca. I Tlatelolchi, vedendo morto il loro Re, tosto si scompigliarono, e procurarono di salvar la vita colla fuga, passando a traverso de' loro nemici: ma restarono morti in quella piazza quattrocento e sessanta, e tra essi alcuni Uffiziali di considerazione. Dopo questa conquista s' unì perfettamente la Città di Tlatelolco a quella di Messico, e non si considerò più come Città distinta, ma come una parte, o piuttosto come un sobborgo di quella Corte, siccome è presentemente. Il Re di Messico mantenne ivi sempre un Governatore, ed i Tlatelolchi oltre al tributo, che annualmente pagavano alla Corona di frumentone, di robe da vestire, d'armi, e d'armadure, erano obbligati a rifare il tempio di Huitznahuac, ogni volta che bisognasse. Non sappiamo, se i Quauhpanchesi, i Huexotzinchi, ed i Matlatzinchi, che s' erano confederati co' Tlatelolchi si trovarono in fatti in questa guerra. Degli altri Alleati
e: altogether unjust: for Moquihuix did not fail in the duties of a general Bk. IV. and of a king, since he ought not to expose his own life as much as the soldiers theirs, in order to be able to be more useful to them by counsel and by voice. Meanwhile the Mexicans advanced as far as the stairway of the temple and, climbing it, reached the upper court, from which Moquihuix encouraged his people and defended himself like a desperate man; but a Mexican captain named Quetzalhua threw him down the stairs with a shove, (l) and some soldiers, taking the corpse on their arms, presented it to Axayacatl, who, opening its chest, tore out the heart. A horrible act, but performed without horror, being too common in their sacrifices. Thus ended the brave Moquihuix, and with him the little monarchy of the Tlatelolcas, governed by four kings in the space of about a hundred and eighteen years. The Tlatelolcas, seeing their king dead, at once fell into disorder and tried to save their lives by flight, passing through the midst of their enemies; but four hundred and sixty were left dead in that square, and among them some officers of note. After this conquest the city of Tlatelolco was perfectly united to that of Mexico, and was no longer considered a distinct city, but as a part, or rather a suburb, of that court, as it is at present. The king of Mexico always kept a governor there, and the Tlatelolcas, besides the tribute of maize, clothing, arms, and armor that they paid annually to the crown, were obliged to rebuild the temple of Huitznahuac whenever it should be needed. We do not know whether the people of Cuauhpanco, the Huexotzincas, and the Matlatzincas, who had confederated with the Tlatelolcas, were in fact present in this war. As for the other allies,

o: dicono gli Storici, che essendo arrivati al soccorso de' Tlatelolchi, quando era già morto Moquihuix, e terminata la guerra, se ne tornarono senza far nulla. Tosto, che Axajacatl si vide vittorioso, condannò all' estremo supplizio Pojahuitl, ed Ehecatzitzimitl, amendue Tlatelolchi, per essere stati quelli, che più caldamente aveano animati i loro Cittadini contro i Messicani, ed indi a poco fece morire i Signori di Xochimilco, di Cuitlahuac, di Colhuacan, di Huitzilopochco, ed altri, per essersi confederati co' suoi nemici. [margin: §. 17. Nuove conquiste, e morte d'Axajacatl.] Per vendicarsi poi de' Matlatzinchi, Nazione numerosa e possente, stabilita nella Valle di Toluca, e non ancor sottoposta a' Messicani, pubblicò la guerra contro loro, ed uscendo da Messico insieme co' due Re alleati, prese nel passare i luoghi di Atlapolco, e di Xalatlauhco, e poi nella stessa Valle conquistò Toluca, Tetenanco, Metepec, Tzinacantepec, Calimaja, ed altri luoghi della parte meridionale della Valle, restando d' allora innanzi la Nazione tributaria della Corona di Messico. Dopo qualche tempo ritornò nella medesima Provincia per conquistare ancora la parte settentrionale della Valle, appellata oggidì Valle d' Ixtlahuacan, e principalmente Xiquipilco, Città e stato considerabile degli Otomiti, il cui Signore, chiamato Tlilcuezpalin, era famoso per la sua bravura. Axajacatl, il quale ancor vantava il suo coraggio, volle duellare con esso lui nella battaglia, che presentò a' Xiquipilchesi; ma la riuscita fu al medesimo Axajacatl funesta; poichè ebbe una grave ferita nella coscia, e sopravvenendo due Capitani Otomiti, lo gettarono a più colpi in terra, e l' avrebbono fatto prigione, se certi giovani Messicani, vedendo il loro Re in sì grave pericolo, non gli avessero coraggiosamente salvato la libertà, e la vita. Malgrado d' una tal disgrazia, ottennero i Messicani una compita vittoria, e fecero, per quel che dicono i loro Storici, undici mila e sessanta prigionieri, tra i quali e lo stesso Tlilcuezpalin, e que' due Capitani, che aveano assalito il Re. Con questa gloriosa vittoria aggiunse Axajacatl alla Corona Xiquipilco, Xocotitlan, Atlacomolco, e tutti gli altri luoghi, che gli mancavano di quell' amena valle.
e: the historians say that, having arrived to the relief of the Tlatelolcas Bk. IV. when Moquihuix was already dead and the war ended, they went back without doing anything. As soon as Axayacatl saw himself victorious, he condemned to the extreme penalty Poyahuitl and Ehecatzitzimitl, both Tlatelolcas, for having been the ones who had most warmly stirred up their fellow citizens against the Mexicans, and shortly afterward he put to death the lords of Xochimilco, Cuitlahuac, Colhuacan, Huitzilopochco, and others, for having confederated with his enemies. § 17. To avenge himself next on the Matlatzincas, a numerous and powNew conquests, and erful nation settled in the Valley of Toluca and not yet subject to the death of Axayacatl. Mexicans, he declared war on them, and setting out from Mexico together with the two allied kings, he took in passing the places of Atlapolco and Xalatlauhco, and then in the same valley conquered Toluca, Tetenanco, Metepec, Tzinacantepec, Calimaya, and other places in the southern part of the valley, the nation remaining from then on tributary to the crown of Mexico. After some time he returned to the same province to conquer also the northern part of the valley, today called the Valley of Ixtlahuaca, and chiefly Xiquipilco, a city and considerable state of the Otomis, whose lord, named Tlilcuezpalin, was famous for his bravery. Axayacatl, who still boasted of his courage, wished to fight a duel with him in the battle that he offered to the people of Xiquipilco; but the outcome was disastrous to Axayacatl himself; for he received a severe wound in the thigh, and two Otomi captains, coming upon him, threw him to the ground with several blows and would have taken him prisoner, had not certain young Mexicans, seeing their king in such grave danger, courageously saved his liberty and his life. In spite of such a misfortune, the Mexicans gained a complete victory, and took, according to their historians, eleven thousand and sixty prisoners, among them Tlilcuezpalin himself and those two captains who had assailed the king. By this glorious victory Axayacatl added to the crown Xiquipilco, Xocotitlan, Atlacomulco, and all the other places of that pleasant valley that he still lacked.

o: Tosto che risanò Axajacatl della ferita, la quale per altro lo storpiò di una gamba per tutto il resto della sua vita, fece un gran pranzo a' Re alleati, ed a' Magnati Messicani, nel qual fece morire Tlilcuezpalin, ed i due suddetti Capitani otomiti. Non pareva a quegli uomini inopportuna l' esecuzion d' un supplizio fra le delizie d' un pranzo; imperciocchè avvezzi a spargere il sangue umano aveano cambiato l' orror naturale in ricreazione. Tanto grande è la forza del costume, e tanto è agevole a' nostri animi il rendersi famigliari gli obbietti più orribili! Negli ultimi anni del suo regno, parendogli troppo stretti per la banda di Ponente i termini dell' imperio, uscì di nuovo in campagna per la Valle di Toluca, e passando di là da' monti, conquistò Tochpan, e Tlaximalojan, essendo d' allora in poi questo luogo la frontiera del regno di Michuacan. Indi rivolgendosi verso Levante s' impadronì d'Ocuilla, e di Malacatepec. La morte sopravvenutagli nel decimoterzo anno del suo regno, che fu il 1477. dell' era volgare, interruppe il corso delle sue vittorie. Fu assai guerriere, e severo nel punire i trasgressori delle leggi dal suo Antecessore pubblicate. Lasciò da parecchie mogli un gran numero di figliuoli, fra i quali il celebre Motezuma II., di cui fra poco ragioneremo. [margin: §. 18. Tizoc Re settimo di Messico.] In luogo d'Axajacatl fu eletto Tizoc, fratello maggior di lui, il quale esercitato avea la carica di General d'esercito. s1 Non sappiamo, dove fosse la sua prima spedizione, per procurarsi delle vittime necessarie per la sua incoronazione. Il suo regno fu breve, ed oscuro. Nondimeno nella dipintura decima della raccolta di Mendoza si rappresentano quattordici Città da lui sottomesse, fra le quali vi sono Toluca, e Tecaxic, che per essersi ribellate alla Corona, bisognò
e: As soon as Axayacatl recovered from the wound, which, however, crippled Bk. IV. one of his legs for the rest of his life, he gave a great banquet to the allied kings and to the Mexican grandees, at which he put to death Tlilcuezpalin and the two aforesaid Otomi captains. The carrying out of a punishment amid the delights of a banquet did not seem inopportune to those men; for, accustomed to shed human blood, they had changed their natural horror into recreation. So great is the force of custom, and so easy is it for our minds to make the most horrible objects familiar to themselves! In the last years of his reign, finding the limits of the empire too narrow on the west side, he went out again on campaign through the Valley of Toluca and, passing beyond the mountains, conquered Tochpan and Tlaximaloyan, this place being from then on the frontier of the kingdom of Michoacán. Then, turning toward the east, he took possession of Ocuillan and Malacatepec. Death, which came upon him in the thirteenth year of his reign, which was 1477 of the common era, interrupted the course of his victories. He was very warlike, and severe in punishing those who transgressed the laws published by his predecessor. He left by several wives a great number of sons, among whom was the famous Moctezuma II, of whom we shall shortly speak. In place of Axayacatl, Tizoc, his elder brother, who had exercised the office § 18. Tizoc, seventh king of general of the army, was elected. (m) We do not know where his first expe‐ of Mexico. dition was, undertaken to procure the victims necessary for his coronation. His reign was short and obscure. Nevertheless, in the tenth painting of the Mendoza Collection fourteen cities are represented as subdued by him, among them Toluca and Tecaxic, which, having rebelled against the crown, had to be reconquered

o: riconquistare, Chillan, e Jancuitlan nel paese de' Mixtechi, Mazatlan; Tlapan, e Tamapachco. Torquemada fa menzione d' una vittoria da lui ottenuta sopra Tlacotepec. [margin: §. 19. Guerra fra i Tezcucani, e gli Huexotzinchi.] Nel tempo di questo Re accadde la guerra tra i Tezcucani, e gli Huexotzinchi. Cotal guerra ebbe la sua origine dall' ambizione de' Principi fratelli del Re Nezahualpilli, i quali quantunque contenti si mostrarono sul principio della esaltazione del loro fratello minore, essendosi poi raffreddata la memoria del loro defunto Padre, e non più sofferendo il vedersi sottomessi a colui, cui credevano dover comandare pel dritto della età, macchinarono contro lui una segreta congiura. Per l' esecuzione de' lor perversi disegni invitarono prima i Chalchesi, ch' erano i più pronti a sì fatti delitti; ma avendo fallito tutti i mezzi da essi adoperati, sollecitarono pel medesimo fine gli Huexotzinchi. Nezahualpilli, avvisato d' una tal congiura, allestì senza indugio un buon esercito, e marciò per andar contro gli Huexotzinchi. Il Generale di quello stato avea indagati tutti i contrassegni del Re Nezahualpilli, per portar contro esso lui tutti i suoi colpi, ed aveva anche promesso de' premj a chiunque glielo consegnasse o vivo, o morto. Non mancò chi il facesse sapere al Re: onde questi prima d' entrar nella battaglia mutò le sue vesti ed insegne con quelle d' un suo Capitano. Questo sventurato uffiziale, essendo stato creduto lo stesso Re, fu subito sopraffatto dalla moltitudine, ed ucciso. Mentre contro di lui si sfogava la loro rabbia, Nezahualpilli diede addosso al Generale Huexotzinca, e l' uccise non senza grave rischio d' esser anch' egli ammazzato da' soldati, che vennero a soccorrere il loro Generale. I Tezcucani, i quali aveano preso lo stesso sbaglio degli Huexotzinchi, per non esser consapevoli del cambiamento delle vesti, aveano cominciato a disanimarsi; ma ora conoscendolo, concorsero alla difesa di lui, e dopo avere sconfitti i suoi nemici, saccheggiarono la Città di Huexotzinco, e carichi di spoglie se ne tornarono a Tezcuco. Niente dicono gli Storici del fine, che ebbero i Principi autori della congiura. Può credersi,
e: Chillan, and Yancuitlan in the country of the Mixtecs, Mazatlan, Bk. IV. Tlapan, and Tamapachco. Torquemada makes mention of a victory won by him over Tlacotepec. § 19. In the time of this king there occurred the war between the War between the Texcocans and the Huexotzincas. That war had its origin in the ambiTexcocans and the Huexotzincas. tion of the princes, brothers of King Nezahualpilli, who, though they showed themselves content at the beginning with the exaltation of their younger brother, the memory of their dead father having afterward cooled, and no longer able to bear seeing themselves subject to one whom they believed they ought to command by right of age, plotted a secret conspiracy against him. For the execution of their perverse designs they first invited the Chalcas, who were the readiest for such misdeeds; but having failed in all the means they had employed, they solicited for the same end the Huexotzincas. Nezahualpilli, informed of such a conspiracy, equipped without delay a good army and marched to go against the Huexotzincas. The general of that state had ascertained all the marks of King Nezahualpilli, in order to direct all his blows against him, and had even promised rewards to anyone who should deliver him over to him alive or dead. There was someone who made it known to the king; whereupon he, before entering the battle, exchanged his garments and insignia for those of one of his captains. This unfortunate officer, having been taken for the king himself, was at once overwhelmed by the multitude and killed. While they were venting their rage upon him, Nezahualpilli fell upon the Huexotzinca general and killed him, not without grave risk of being killed himself by the soldiers who came to the aid of their general. The Texcocans, who had made the same mistake as the Huexotzincas, not being aware of the change of garments, had begun to lose heart; but now, recognizing him, they rushed to his defense, and after having routed his enemies, they sacked the city of Huexotzinco and, laden with spoils, returned to Texcoco. The historians say nothing of the end that the princes, authors of the conspiracy, met with. It may be believed,

o: che fossero uccisi nella battaglia, o pure si salvassero colla fuga dal gastigo, che meritavano. Nezahualpilli, il quale poco innanzi s' era fabbricato un nuovo palagio, fece ancora per lasciar un eterno monumento della sua vittoria, construire un muro, che tanto spazio di terra rinchiudesse, quanto era quello, che occupavano gli Huexotzinchi, allorchè vennero alla difesa del loro Generale, e diede a quel luogo lo stesso nome del giorno, in cui s' ottenne la vittoria. Così procuravano render immortale il loro nome, e la gloria delle loro azioni quelli, che da molti son creduti niente curarsi dell' avvenire. [margin: §. 20. Nozze del Re Nezahualpilli; con due Signore Messicane.] Aveva già allora il Re di Tezcuco parecchie mogli di case nobilissime; ma niuna era stata da lui dichiarata Regina, riservando tal' onore per quella, che voleva togliere dalla famiglia Real di Messico. Domandolla al Re Tizoc, e questi gli diede una sua nipote, figlia di Tzotzocatzin. Celebraronsi queste nozze in Tezcuco con gran concorso di Nobiltà delle due Corti. Aveva questa Signora una sorella dotata di singolar bellezza, che si appellava Xocotzin. Amavansi tanto amendue, che non potendo separarsi, ottenne la nuova Regina da suo Padre il permesso di condur seco a Tezcuco sua sorella. Colla frequente vista, e col trattare spesso s' invaghì tanto il Re della sua bella cognata, che determinò sposarla, ed esaltarla ancora alla dignità di Regina. While Nezahualpilli was seeking to multiply his descendants, enjoying great peace and tranquillity in his kingdom, some of his feuda‐ § 21. tories were plotting the death of the king of Mexico. Techotlalla, lord Tragic death of King Tizoc. of Iztapalapan, either resentful over some displeasure received or impatient of Tizoc’s domination, conceived the wicked design of making an attempt on his life, and would reveal it to no one except to such as seemed to him capable of carrying it out. He and Maxtlaton, lord of Tlachco, agreed on the manner of executing so dangerous a crime. The historians do not agree on this point. Some say that they made use of certain witches, and that these by sorcery took his life; but this seems to me a popular fable. Others affirm that they found a way of giving him poison. However that may be, it is certain that their plot succeeded. Tizoc was killed in the fifth year of his reign, in 1482 of the common era. He was a circumspect man, grave and severe, like his predecessors and successors, in the punishment of offenders. Since in his time the power and opulence of that crown were already so great, he undertook to build for the tutelary god of the nation a temple that in size and magnificence should surpass all the temples of that country, and to this end he had prepared infinite materials and had even begun the building, when death came to upset his designs. The Mexicans, well aware that the death of their king had not been natural, wished to avenge it before proceeding to a new election. Their inquiries were so thorough that in a short time they discovered the authors of the attempt and put them to death in the great square § 22. of Mexico in the presence of the two allied kings and of the Mexican Ahuitzotl, eighth and Texcocan nobility. IV. brated the dedication of a new temple, called Tlacatecco, in which the prisoners taken in the earlier wars were sacrificed; but the joy of that festival was disturbed by the burning of the temple of Tlillan. Thus this king passed his reign in continual wars until 1496, in which year the war against Atlixco took place. The entry of the Mexican army into this valley was so sudden that the first notice the people of Atlixco had of it was that which they received through their eyes on seeing them enter. They took up arms at once for their defense; but not finding themselves with forces sufficient to resist for long, they asked help of the Huexotzincas, their neighbors. When the ambassadors of Atlixco arrived at Huexotzinco, a famous captain named Toltecatl, whose great courage was in no way inferior to the extraordinary strength of his arm, was playing ball. As soon as he learned the news of the Mexican army, he left the game to go to Atlixco with the auxiliary troops, and, entering the battle unarmed, to display his bravery and to show the contempt he felt for his enemies, he struck down with his fists the first Mexican who presented himself, and took his arms, with which he made great slaughter. The Mexicans, unable to overcome the resistance of their enemies, abandoned the field and returned to Mexico covered with ignominy. The Huexotzincas, to reward the singular prowess of Toltecatl, made him head of their republic. This had been subjected to the dominion of the Mexicans, whose arms they had provoked with their insults; but since the conquered do not bear the yoke of the conqueror except when they cannot shake it off, every time the Huexotzincas found themselves with forces sufficient to resist, they rebelled, and the same happened with the greater part of the provinces subjected by force of arms to the crown of Mexico; whence it was necessary that the Mexican army should be in continual motion to reconquer what the king was losing. Toltecatl accepted the office conferred on him; but

The priests and other ministers of the temples, abusing their authority, entered the houses of private persons and carried off the maize and the turkeys that were there, and committed other excesses unbecoming to their dignity. Toltecatl wished to put a stop to it; but the priests took up arms. The people partly sided with them, and partly opposed their violence, and between these two factions a war broke out, which, like all other civil wars, caused very grave evils. Toltecatl, weary of ruling so unruly a people, or fearing to perish in the tempest, withdrew from the city with other nobles and, crossing the mountains, betook himself to Tlalmanalco. The governor of this city gave prompt notice of it to the king of Mexico, and he at once put to death all those fugitives in punishment of their rebellion, and had their bodies carried to Huexotzinco to frighten the rebels. § 25. In 1498 it seemed to the king of Mexico that for lack of water the New inundation of Mexico.  navigation  of the lake had become difficult, and he wished to increase that water with the other from the spring of Huitzilopochco, which the people of Coyoacán used, and he summoned Tzotzomatzin, lord of Coyoacán, to give him his orders. Tzotzomatzin represented to him that that spring was not perennial: that at times the water failed, and at times came in such abundance that it might cause some damage to the court. Ahuitzotl, thinking that Tzotzomatzin’s reasons were mere pretexts to excuse himself from doing what had been commanded him, insisted on his first order; and seeing that man persist in the difficulty he had put forward, he dismissed him in anger, and afterward had him put to death. This is usually the reward of good counsels, when princes obstinate in some caprice will not listen to the sincere remonstrances of their faithful subjects. Ahuitzotl, unwilling by any means to abandon his project, had a great and ample aqueduct () made from Coyoacán to Mexico, and through it was conducted the

(q) With such solemnity the water arrived at Mexico; but it was not long before the general joy was changed into weeping; for the rains of that year having been extraordinarily abundant, the water of the lake rose so much that it flooded the city, all the streets were full of boats, and some houses collapsed. One day, the king being in a lower room of his palace, the water entered it so suddenly and in such quantity that, hastening in his fear to go out by the door, which was low, he gave himself such a violent blow on the head that after some time it caused his death. Afflicted by the evils of the inundation and by the clamors of the people, he called to his aid the king of Acolhuacan, who without delay had the dike repaired that, on the counsel of his father Nezahualcoyotl, had been built in the reign of Moctezuma. Scarcely were the Mexicans freed from the evil of the inundation when in the following year they had to suffer that of the scarcity of grain, the maize having been spoiled by the excessive abundance of water; but in this same year they had the good fortune to discover in the valley of Mexico a quarry of tetzontli, which has been so useful for the buildings of that great city. The king at once began to use this kind of stone in the temples, and in imitation of him private persons in their houses. Besides this the king had all
